nodes.goal: STEP 1 — UE5.8.3 scalability verify on T1000: 1080p medium, volumetric fog + storm scene, PASS = >=30fps. Verdict decides Unreal vs Godot.

STEP 2 — SPEC LOCK: full design doc (systems, keeper-record mechanics, storm/lens/oil interactions, island layout, endings, critic rubric) + derived asset list with provenance. On disk before any code.
STEP 3 — Blender asset phase via Python API: island+coastline, lighthouse ext+int, keeper character, boat, props, storm sky. All original.
STEP 4 — Engine build phase: third-person controller, storm/weather, job-matters mechanics (lens->beam, oil->survival, wrecks->reefs), keeper-record log, save/load, menus, tutorial, settings.
STEP 5 — Critic loop: up to 3 rounds, play + multi-viewpoint screenshots, self-score AND qa-critic score, binding = lower, PASS at 8.5+.
STEP 6 — Delivery: playable build + design doc + scored screenshots + keeper-record demo + round history, committed.
STEP 1 DONE — UE5.8.3 PASS on T1000: 52fps steady @1080p medium with volumetric fog storm scene (clouds off); clouds cost 15ms — banned by budget law. Verdict: Unreal.
